test_title: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-1 (Held On: 28 Nov, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Two pipes of length 1.5 meters and 1.2 meters are to be cut into equal pieces without leaving any extra length. What is the greatest length of pieces of the same size that can be cut from both pipes?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the greatest common length, calculate the HCF of the given values.

Lengths are 1.5 and 1.2.

Ignore decimal: HCF(15, 12) = 3.

Place decimal back: 0.3.

**∴ Answer = 0.3 meter**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of Pipe 1 = 1.5 meters

Length of Pipe 2 = 1.2 meters

**Formula used:**

Greatest length of pieces = HCF(Length₁, Length₂)

 Pipe 1: 1.5 m 
• 
• 
• 
• Pipe 2: 1.2 m 
• 
• 
• 0.3m 0.3m 0.3m 0.3m 0.3m Greatest Piece Length = 0.3 m 

**Calculations:**

Convert the lengths to a common unit to avoid decimals (centimeters):

⇒ Length 1 = 1.5 × 100 = 150 cm

⇒ Length 2 = 1.2 × 100 = 120 cm

Find the HCF of 150 and 120:

⇒ 150 = 30 × 5

⇒ 120 = 30 × 4

⇒ HCF(150, 120) = 30 cm

Convert back to meters:

⇒ 30 cm = 30 ÷ 100 = 0.3 meter

**∴ The correct answer is 0.3 meter (Option 2).**
